doc.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

chapter: Nellie Lutcher and Lambert, Hendricks & Ross
title: The trio's personalities and Dave Lambert's temper
summary: Jon and Dave clashed offstage, Annie stayed above it, and Dave cursed out a stewardess.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: What were they like, as the three personalities? Did they mesh pretty well?

Not in my estimation. Well on stage they did, yeah, they meshed fine on stage. Jon and Dave were at each other’s throats a good part of the time. Their personalities were different. They clashed. Annie was above it all. She was regular. She didn’t care what they did, as long as they left her alone to do her thing. That’s off the stage. Dave was

intense, curious, he could fly into a rage. I remember one time we were coming from Pittsburgh, Dave and I caught a flight home. My kids were small and I was on the road so much. And it was Christmas time and I didn’t want to have to drive home the next morning from Pittsburgh, that’s another whole day wasted. So Dave and I rushed to the airport and caught a flight home. And we were the last people to get on the plane. And the plane is taxiing away from the gate almost to the runway and everybody’s supposed to be in their seats with their seatbelt on and trays folded up. I don’t even remember if they had trays in those days. But anyway Dave is stuffing stuff in the overhead rack. He’s standing in the aisle and he’s getting himself settled. And the stewardess comes rushing up, “Sir, you’re supposed to be seated, the seat belt sign is on” blah blah blah. And he cursed her out so badly, I couldn’t believe it.
If he did that now he’d be tossed right off.

Yeah how about that. It’s like Charles Davis said the other day, he said, “Well look man, if you got to meet your friend Jack on the plane and then you meet up on the plane, just don’t say ‘hi Jack.’”
Well I laughed, I said that’s a good point. I’ll take that seriously.
